# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–12 (Complete – Updated 106)

## Setting and Time
- **Current Period**: Winter of third year in Mirecombe hill farms; frost on hedges; road rutted and puddled after thaw. Earlier: evening at Brighton following Dobbin's arrival; fine brilliant moonlight night of May, warm and balmy. Army ordered to Belgium before week's end; mobilization imminent from Chatham. Three weeks before French Emperor likely attacks.
- **Primary Locations**: London (Russell Square, Thames Street counting-house, Slaughters' hotel, Gray's Inn Square, Cavendish Square fine hotel), Brighton (George-Amelia honeymoon, Rawdon-Rebecca residence, Ship Inn, bathing machines on beach), Mirecombe (Seena Orlwood—drowned in flood; Pebin Wexwood, Maric Lindson, Rozek Hollwood, Halan Hollwood, Isbin Hollwood, Orvie, Nynelle Stenworth, Seena Hollett, Brenelle and Orvie Hollett, Thidrek Corrett, Feten Lindner, children of Quenwick, Old Maric, Ilena Orlwood, Orrine, Staveton), Coldcombe hill farms, Dunholt village (Daric Brackwood, Thivie, Feena Stenworth, Cotho Brackwood, daughter Dalde Brackwood born), Chatham (embarkation point), Harwich (shipping departure point), Fulham (Mrs. Sedley's house, Mr. and Mrs. Clapp, Irish servant Miss Flannigan, Mr. Clapp gardening), Belgium (destination), Ghent, Brussels (military balls planned), France (coast visible from Brighton)

## Main Characters

**Captain William Dobbin** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Role in Marriage**: Primary architect of reconciliation; convinced both to proceed; urged George before Belgium orders; presented gold chain and watch to Amelia; groomsman
- **Confrontation with John Osborne - UNSUCCESSFUL**: Entered City counting-house; received cordial welcome; revealed Belgium deployment; urged reconciliation. Osborne erupted calling Amelia "swindling old bankrupt's daughter"; accused Dobbin of setting George up. Dobbin departed; later sent note to Osborne
- **Brighton Arrival and Actions**: Arrived via Slaughters' hotel; imparted Belgium news to Ensign Stubble; witnessed his tears; dined with officers at theatre box. At Ship Inn: assumed "jovial and rattling manner" to hide feelings upon seeing Amelia; made clumsy compliments
- **In Dobbin's Room with George - COMPLETED**: Delivered lawyer's letter from Mr. Osborne containing disinheritance notice. George erupted in rage, blaming Dobbin; complained about financial ruin. Dobbin replied calmly; offered personal financial support; promised not to forget godson in will. George forgave Dobbin
- **Internal Conflict Intensified**: Deeply troubled by guilt over hastening marriage; feels his own unendurable suspense drove him to crush uncertainty; considers himself traitor to both father and son. Secret adoration of Amelia is now his "greatest privilege and hope of life"; privately resolved he would not have let her go to Belgium if married to her; will not remonstrate with George as master
- **Reputation**: "Greatly respected in the regiment, as the best officer and the cleverest man in it"; backed young Stubble's courage
- **Evening Dinner at Brighton - COMPLETED**: Assumed character of "rattle"; described army in Belgium with accounts of fetes, fashion; described Mrs. Major O'Dowd packing wardrobe with epaulets in tea canister and yellow turban. When Rebecca announced intention to go to Belgium on staff, Dobbin flushed red, objected about danger, became "very confused and silent." Agreed with George and Jos to move party to London next day
- **Cavendish Square Hotel - CURRENT**: Attempted to remonstrate after dinner against extravagance of turtle and champagne for archbishop; George dismissed concerns, declared wife shall travel like lady. Dobbin walked home to Slaughters' after seeing Amelia off in coach; mused it would be delightful to be in hackney-coach with Mrs. Osborne
- **Knowledge of Amelia's Opinion**: Knows Amelia considers him plain, awkward, ungainly; acquiesces humbly; acknowledges "a time came when she knew him better" but that was distant

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Status - MARRIED, DISINHERITED**: Married Amelia late April without father's consent; honeymoon at Brighton; disinherited by father's lawyer letter (determination "final and irrevocable")
- **Financial Ruin - ACUTE**: Receives £2,000 in 4 percent annuities and £100/year widow's allowance for Amelia; lost £140 to Rawdon Crawley at cards; gave substantial payment to Rawdon from bank-notes and bill on agents; must live on captain's pay
- **Military Orders**: Regiment ordered to Belgium before week's end; faces "great and certain risk"; departing to Chatham, then Harwich for Belgium shipping
- **Response to Amelia's Distress - COMPLETED**: Parried question about foreign service with melancholy; said disinheritance was his concern; gave her letter to read. Upon her cheerful acceptance and quoting "Wapping Old Stairs," praised her resolution; patted her under chin; agreed lady should bear him company to Belgium with Mrs. O'Dowd as chaperone. Evening dinner: excitement of campaign counteracted depression; applauded Amelia's resolution. Received crumpled family-note from Rawdon asking for money; gave considerable bank-notes and bill on agents. Held council of war with Jos and Dobbin; agreed general move to London next day
- **Departure from Brighton - EXECUTED**: Left Brighton for London in Jos's carriage
- **Cavendish Square Hotel - CURRENT**: Took suite of splendid rooms at fine hotel in Cavendish Square with magnificently furnished table and black silent waiters. Did honours with princely air to Jos and Dobbin. Pooh-poohed wine and bullied waiters; declared wife shall travel like lady "as long as there's a shot in the locker." Evening: sent Amelia to Fulham in coach with valet while he went to half-price theatre to see Mr. Kean perform Shylock. Is great lover of drama and performed high-comedy characters in garrison theatricals. Currently drinking claret; had business that night

**Amelia Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Status - MARRIED, BRIDE**: Married to George late April; one week into marriage
- **Emotional Crisis - RESOLVED TEMPORARILY**: Initially troubled by Rebecca's wit and accomplishments; misgives about Rebecca; observed George suffering ennui; tormented by guilt about forcing marriage and causing disinheritance; blames herself for neglecting mother. **Face cleared as she read** disinheritance letter; idea of sharing poverty with beloved is far from disagreeable and actually pleasant
- **Resolution to Go to Belgium - EXECUTED**: Cried with "greatest spirit" determination to accompany George; George applauded, called her "termagant of a wife." Bitterness of parting "juggled away"
- **Departure Preparations - EXECUTED**: Rose early morning; packed little trunks with "greatest alacrity" while George lay in bed; "only too glad" to perform office herself
- **Cavendish Square Hotel - CURRENT**: For first time presided at table with "exceeding shyness and timidity"; unaware turtle tureen contents (calipash/calipee); timidly expressed wish to visit mother at Fulham; George granted permission with grumbling. Put on bonnet and shawl with "utmost eagerness and pleasure"
- **Visit to Fulham - CURRENT**: Made "little disappointed curtsey" after looking vainly into George's face when he declined accompanying her. Went sadly down great staircase; Dobbin handed her into hackney-coach. Mother Mrs. Sedley clasped her to heart with "all maternal eagerness and affection," ran out of door weeping; old Mr. Clapp shrank back alarmed in shirt-sleeves; Irish servant-lass rushed up smiling "God bless you"; Amelia could hardly walk along flags
- **Emotional Spiral - CURRENT**: Went upstairs to little room occupied before marriage; sank into chair as if old friend; fell to thinking over past week and life beyond. Already looking sadly back; always pining for something which when obtained brought doubt and sadness rather than pleasure. Recalled fondly image of George worshipped before marriage; did not own to self how different real man was; reflected on Rebecca's "twinkling green eyes and baleful smile"; indulged in usual mood of selfish brooding and listless melancholy. Looked at white bed yearned to sleep in it; thought with terror of great funereal damask pavilion awaiting her at grand hotel. Knelt by bedside seeking consolation; love had been her faith hitherto; sad, bleeding disappointed heart began to feel want of another consoler

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca Rawdon Crawley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Secretly married to Rawdon Crawley; recently at Brighton; still dunned by creditors; relies on Miss Crawley's relenting
- **Miss Crawley Reconciliation - FAILED**: Successfully reconciled with Miss Briggs on beach after bathing. Briggs assured conversation would reach Miss Crawley within hours. Rebecca initiated letter-writing campaign: Rawdon dictated (Rebecca composed) tender letter to Miss Crawley expressing humble acceptance of marriage to poor woman, desire for reconciliation before departing England, reluctance to quit country without kind farewell from her. **Miss Crawley's Response - REJECTION**: Upon Briggs reading epistle, Miss Crawley laughed, recognized Rebecca's composition not Rawdon's (noting his letters always full of bad spelling, dashes, bad grammar, requests for money); concluded "that little serpent of a governess who rules him"; believes all relatives "want me dead, and are hankering for my money." Despite Briggs' reports of letter content touching her, Miss Crawley remained unmoved
- **Meeting Between Rawdon and Miss Crawley - EXECUTED, DISAPPOINTING OUTCOME**: Briggs warned Rawdon to wait on Cliff when Miss Crawley took air in chair. They met; Miss Crawley held out couple of fingers with "smiling and good-humoured air." Rawdon "turned as red as scarlet, and wrung off Briggs's hand, so great was his rapture and his confusion." Miss Crawley subsequently mused upon meeting: remarked to Briggs "Rawdon is getting very fat and old...His nose has become red, and he is exceedingly coarse in appearance. His marriage to that woman has hopelessly vulgarised him...he smelt of gin abominably."
- **Miss Crawley's Refusal - FINAL**: Declined to receive Rebecca; instructed Briggs to write letter stating her health too delicate for family discussions or interviews; thanked Rawdon for coming to Brighton; instructed him to call upon her lawyer's in Gray's Inn Square for communication. Letter's reference to lawyer provided Rawdon some consolation after initial disappointment
- **Monetary Scheme - EXECUTED**: Sent crumpled family-note to Rawdon requesting money from "Cupid" (George) before he departs; Rawdon successfully extracted considerable payment from George in bank-notes and bill on agents. Rebecca remarked to Rawdon: "A comfortable inn in Brighton is better than a spunging-house in Chancery Lane"; noted Mr. Jos and Captain Cupid are better companions than sheriff's officers
- **Debtor Evasion - EXECUTED**: In consequence of repeated visits of aides-de-camp of Sheriff of Middlesex, Rawdon and Rebecca did not return to lodgings at Brompton but put up at inn. Rebecca wisely packed all their chief valuables and sent them off under care of George's servant, who went in charge of trunks on coach back to London
- **Departure to London - EXECUTED**: Rawdon and Rebecca returned to London by same conveyance next day after Brighton stay. Rebecca visited old Mrs. Sedley's house at Fulham to see Amelia and Brighton friends
- **Current Status - LONDON**: Lighted on Amelia's mind with "twinkling green eyes and baleful smile" filling her with dismay; in London with furious Rawdon (outcome of Miss Crawley's lawyer communication negative but unspecified)

**John Osborne (Old Mr. Osborne)** [MAJOR CHARACTER - FINAL ACTION COMPLETED]
- Wealthy merchant; George's father; savage, determined man
- **Disinheritance - EXECUTED AND COMMUNICATED**: Upon learning George married Amelia, erupted in fury; called George "d---- fool"; denounced Amelia as "swindling old bankrupt's daughter"; accused Dobbin of setting George up. Retreated to study; locked door; retrieved mahogany escritoire containing all George's documents since childhood; examined papers with "curses quivering on livid lips" and "horrid hatred and disappointment"; marked, docketed, catalogued with dates. Commissioned lawyer to draft letter stating determination "final and irrevocable"; George ceases to be member of family; Money expended upon George in minority exceeds entitlement (£2,000 in 4 percent annuities); Mr. Osborne waives all claim upon George's estate. Letter delivered via Mr. Chopper to Dobbin

**Rawdon Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Secretly married to Rebecca; at Brighton; heavily indebted
- **Money Extraction - EXECUTED**: Sent crumpled family-note requesting money from George; successfully extracted considerable payment from George in bank-notes and bill on agents; lost £140 to George at cards
- **Miss Crawley Meeting - COMPLETED, EMOTIONALLY MOVED BUT ULTIMATELY REJECTED**: Warned by Briggs to wait on Cliff; met Miss Crawley when she took air in chair; held out couple of fingers with "smiling and good-humoured air." Rawdon "turned as red as scarlet, and wrung off Briggs's hand, so great was his rapture and his confusion." Walked by side of chair to Miss Crawley's door where Bowls helped her in; wanted to enter but did not. Narrated interview to Rebecca, saying "The old girl has always acted like a trump to me...I felt, you know, rather queer." Miss Crawley's subsequent observations of his appearance and drinking habits deeply offended him
- **Miss Crawley's Lawyer Communication - RECEIVED, FURIOUS RESPONSE**: Went to Gray's Inn Square to visit Miss Crawley's lawyer as instructed in refusal letter; learned his fate (details unstated but implies severe disappointment); "came back furious" to Rebecca in London
- **Current Status**: In London, furious after lawyer visit

**Mr. and Mrs. Sedley (Amelia's Parents)**
- **Current Status**: Mrs. Sedley at Fulham, "very much depressed and tearful, solitary" before Amelia's arrival; ran out of door weeping with "all maternal eagerness and affection" to welcome daughter; thought festive entertainment necessary—prepared muffin and orange marmalade in cut-glass saucer as peculiarly agreeable refreshments for Amelia in "most interesting situation." Dived to kitchen-parlour with Mr. and Mrs. Clapp and Miss Flannigan Irish servant. Old Mr. Sedley in shirt-sleeves gardening; spoke with George's valet about son-in-law, Jos's carriage, horses at Brighton, "infernal traitor Bonaparty" and war; insisted on helping valet with wine; gave half-guinea with toast "to health of your master and mistress, Trotter"

## Critical Facts and Status

- **GEORGE-AMELIA MARRIAGE - LONDON PHASE ACTIVE**: Married late April; one week into marriage. John Osborne's disinheritance "final and irrevocable." Amelia's face cleared reading letter; idea of sharing poverty pleasant. Both determined to go to Belgium together. Currently at Cavendish Square fine hotel; Amelia visited mother at Fulham while George went to theatre; experiencing emotional turmoil and doubt; knelt by bedside seeking spiritual consolation. Preparing departure to Chatham thence Harwich for Belgium shipping with regiment
- **REBECCA-MISS CRAWLEY RECONCILIATION - PERMANENTLY FAILED**: Letter campaign recognized as Rebecca's manipulation; Miss Crawley believes all relatives want her dead for money; briefly kind to Rawdon in person but subsequently disparaged his appearance, character, and drinking; refused to receive Rebecca; sent Rawdon to lawyer (negative outcome); Rebecca now in London with furious Rawdon
- **FINANCIAL CRISIS - ACUTE PHASE**: George disinherited; must live on captain's pay and £100/year widow's allowance for Amelia; gave substantial payment to Rawdon from bank-notes and bill; lost £140 to Rawdon at cards. Rawdon and Rebecca evaded creditors/Sheriff's aides-de-camp; packed valuables sent ahead to London. George declared wife shall travel like lady "as long as there's a shot in the locker"; splendid hotel suite alarmed Dobbin with extravagance
- **MILITARY CRISIS - CAMPAIGN ACTIVATED**: Regiment ordered to Belgium before week's end; soldiers facing "great and certain risk." Party assembling at Chatham, departing Harwick for Belgium. Mrs. Major O'Dowd accompanying; military balls planned at Brussels. Rebecca status regarding General Tufto's staff unclear
- **DEPARTURES EXECUTED**: George-Amelia departed Brighton for London; now at Cavendish Square hotel with Jos and Dobbin. Amelia made evening visit to Fulham mother. Rawdon-Rebecca departed Brighton for London; currently in London
